blocks.content: Recognizing subtle distractors and negative marking traps is the single most effective way to boost your net score.

rows: Look for a single valid counter-example to eliminate
Circle/highlight the negative word immediately upon reading
Mixes units like km/h with m/s or meters with cm
Convert all inputs to standard SI units before solving
Dense paragraph with a simple final question
Skip on first pass; return after securing easy direct marks

items: Always double-check whether the question asks for 'Correct' or 'Incorrect' statements before bubbling your answer.
Beware of unit mismatch traps (e.g., mixing km/h with m/s or meters with centimeters) in numerical problems.
Never spend more than 90 seconds on a single question on your first pass through the exam paper.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Absolute words such as 'always', 'never', and 'only' usually signify incorrect statement options in objective questions.
Negative stems containing keywords like 'NOT', 'EXCEPT', or 'INCORRECT' cause maximum unforced errors if unhighlighted.
Examiners place lengthy speed-bump questions at the beginning of sections to disrupt candidate pacing and focus.
Option choices often include intermediate calculation steps as clever distractor options to trap hasty candidates.
